newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate falls, baht weaker late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate falls, baht weaker late.

text.p: Rising liquidity cut the Thai overnight interbank rate down further to 8.50-9.00 percent on late Tuesday from 9.00-9.50 in the morning, dealers said.
Dealers, however, expect the interbank rate to rebound on Wednesday on higher market demand for funds to meet bank reserve requirements on Thurday.
"Liquidity would be tighter tomorrow because of the coming reserve deadline," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
All commercial banks have to meet Bank of Thailand's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of each month.
The baht eased to 25.504-25.509 to the dollar from 25.498- 25.503 earlier on a stronger dollar abroad, dealers said.

"There were active bids for the dollar today following its rebound against the yen," said a currency dealer. "Activities were limited as some people choose to wait and see the outcome of the U.S. presidential election," a dealer said.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 8.50/ 9.50 satangs per dollar before closing from 8.75-9.25 in the morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate unchanged at 25.48 to the dollar. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
